### Putting Away the Foreign Wives
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/putting-away-the-foreign-wives
Passage: Ezra 10:11
Points:
- Ezra called on the returned exiles to confess their sin and separate from their pagan wives to follow God's will.
- While narrative accounts do not automatically endorse every action, Ezra sought to faithfully apply the Mosaic law within his historical context.
- The community faced a dilemma because the law prohibited pagan idolatry in the land, yet they lacked the civil power to exile or punish violators.
- Under the New Covenant, believers receive further instruction to remain with unbelieving spouses who are willing to stay married.

### Bible Pathway - June 5, 2012
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-june-5-2012.html
Passage: Ezra 10:10-11
Points:
- Ezra confronted the community for compromising with idolatrous practices that had previously caused the exile.
- The people trembled in repentance because the power of God's Word convicted their hearts.
- Obeying God required an agonizing, costly separation from sinful practices to avert divine judgment.
- True spiritual renewal requires believers to decisively separate themselves from worldly compromises.
- While repentance and self-denial can be deeply painful, faithful obedience ultimately produces peace.
